image.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one premium original game-world ENVIRONMENT CONCEPT illustration, a fourth floating island called "Amber Winds" for the family mobile rhythm game Radio Archipelago. This is an artistic design proposal, NOT a Unity screenshot and NOT technical/orthographic projections. One single cohesive image, landscape 3:2 or wide16:9, no panels or collage.

PRIMARY DESIGN: a richly detailed irregular floating archipelago with generous open chasms and massive sculpted stratified grey-brown rocky undersides tapering naturally into clouds. A fresh biome of golden autumn meadows, yellow birch and copper/red maple groves, green moss and deep teal streams; warm ochre/cream plaster radio cottages with turquoise-patinated metal roofs, brass speaker windows and aerials. Three charming full-size wind-radio mills with large elegant copper and cream fabric sails: one main hilltop radio mill, a smaller mill on a side terrace and one distant outcrop mill. Architecture belongs to a cozy original retro-radio technology world, beautifully handcrafted plausible stone foundations, warm wood, copper coils and aerials; no industrial clutter, no steampunk city. Some warm yellow luminous signal-spark glass orbs around a flowered final landing glade, subtle light only.

COMPOSITION AND ROUTE: elevated three-quarter panorama showing the entire substantial main island, thick stone underside and three nearby smaller distinct floating islets. Whole silhouette fits with a sky margin. Foreground lower-left arrival meadow and cottage -> slow rising broad S-curve into open middle of island, past golden trees and a deep OPEN-TOP rocky cleft -> a higher shelf beside the large wind-radio mill -> broad falling bend along the stream and short waterfall -> gentle airborne crossing of the open right chasm via three individually separated small islets and three LARGE, varied, organic billowy cumulus clouds -> curve back toward a foreground-right flower terrace. The layout should support a winding return toward arrival for a repeatable loop without a dull perimeter ring or a sharp hairpin. Use smooth long-radius left-right arcs, changing elevation, no90degree turns. Reveal a generous unobstructed air corridor through the scenery. Keep canopies, mills, roofs, blades, buildings, rock spires and waterfalls BESIDE the playable corridor, not in it. No bridge across the route. No closed or low tunnels. No solid continuous road.

GAMEPLAY INDICATION: ONE clearly legible connected chain of about30–40 thick round turquoise/mint ceramic levitating stepping tiles with fine warm brass rims. A few elongated pill-shaped hold supports in the EXACT same ceramic material/rim style. Tiles hover visibly~0.8m above ground or cross open air, never buried. They indicate the design route, not an exact scored chart. Long supports may curve gently in horizontal plane but must have a straight vertical profile. Plenty of lateral room for steering and camera. The billowy clouds below selected airy crossings are fully volumetric and large enough to support several tile spaces; individual clouds remain separated by visible clear gaps, vary in scale and silhouette, no white sausage or flat carpet. Sparse natural clouds in the surrounding blue-green sky.

ART DIRECTION: gorgeous high-end tactile stylized 3D animated adventure-game environment concept. Natural soft golden-hour sunlight, clear balanced shadows, gentle atmospheric depth, crisp readable silhouette, rich textured materials and carefully sculpted foliage; lush and lovingly detailed yet gameplay-readable, NOT crude low-poly. Bold distinct palette: golden foliage, deep forest teal, patinated turquoise rooftops, copper hardware, cream plaster, natural dark layered rocks. Maintain cool turquoise tiles distinct from gold terrain. Fall season but cheerful and lively for children and teenagers, not spooky or melancholic. Moderate architectural scale: normal human-sized doors and houses, not mini dollhouses. One or two white fabric weather pennants and hanging vines off the stone edges. No characters, animals, UI, labels, arrows, lettering, watermark, logos, contact sheets or view diagrams. The environment is the star.
